entries.detail: The NT (July template) runner started at 11:42, before the freeze, without blind logging. Its progress lines showed per-arm counts after the freeze: P0 1/63, P1 28/59, P4 3/65, P5 2/60 (malformed/edit) at 11:50. No analysis decision depended on them. From 11:52 every governed arm runs with --blind (no outcome counts in logs) and is analysed only when complete.

The final P6/P7 runs at n=300 (out/main/r31b_old_P6.jsonl) completed at 11:42:25, before the freeze. They were not analysed or shown to D before 11:53 UTC, when A's decision_rules.py first computed them. D's predictions for final P6/P7 rest on the interim n=70 only, as PREREG_v1 section 1 states.

Copying rule, 'P7 slips carry " well above P0's 1/16'. Operationalised as: the Wilson 95% CI of the share of P7 malformed edits whose closer contains '"' lies entirely above the P0 share's point estimate. Written after seeing the interim P7 (7/13) and before the first computation of the final P7 share.
P6k: besides P6 at k=2,4 on the 305 set, P6 at k=1 is also run on that set, so the P6 dose curve is paired on the same contexts.

Lag-2 set (k_usable>=2): the 146 gate contexts with k_usable>=2, plus 104 contexts from the random order position 600+ (outside the gate and held-out halves) with their own P0 and P1k1, for 250 in total (data/ids_lag2.txt).
r-dose: copies 2..r of the corrupted call + ADK error carry no thought (reasoning). The first copy keeps the original thought. Repeats get unique tool_call ids.

P4' (the replaced call re-rendered canonically in the model's own emitted order + its true success response) is byte-identical to P0 in 297/300 gate contexts (out/p4prime_identity.json). P4' is run only on the 3 differing contexts; on the gate set its removal is 100% by construction. Its informative test is A2 (P4'-MAP).

PREREG_v1 section 5 names P(malformed | next call is edit_file) primary for the governed analyses; its anchors p1=0.462 and p0=0.057 are conditional. UPGRADE_PLAN section 2 and the PI name the unconditional ITT rate primary. A reports both for every contrast. Rule D-M is computed on the prereg's primary (conditional) with the unconditional version beside it. The plan rules that name the unconditional estimand use it. Where a rule names neither, both are reported.

entries.type: design detail, decided blind (PI decision on observation masking)
entries.detail: P's harness masks the oldest tool outputs once a prompt would exceed 22,000 tokens. The 2 most recent turns are never masked. A masked output is replaced by the fixed text '[This earlier tool output was removed to keep the conversation within the context limit.]', and the reasoning of that assistant turn is set to null. A's v1 pool and meta builders read a tool result's status from its text, so they would have scored every masked edit result as a success. PI decision, implemented in sample_pools_v2.py and build_contexts_P.py v1.1 (sha256 60025bef… and b7e1fb5d…, frozen 15:51:30Z beside the v1 hashes in out/confirmatory_script_hashes_v1.txt): (1) eligibility and k_usable use each context's history_tool_status (the status as executed), never the rendered text; (2) A1, A2 (and A1k2 under the shortfall rule) exclude every state in which an injection target's tool result is masked in the original context: the most recent prior edit for A1 (k = 1 arms) and the 2 or 4 most recent prior edits for A1k2 or A2 (P6k). Otherwise P0 and P1/P5/P6 would also differ in masked versus unmasked; (3) B1 is unchanged, because its eligibility uses no tool status; (4) POOLS_MANIFEST.json reports per pool the states eligible before rule 2 and the number rule 2 excludes. Same release: every accepted state records its split. The Verified-only subset of each accepted pool is written to pools/verified_only/ for the pre-specified Verified-only sensitivity analysis (PI entry 15:27). confirm_v2_analysis.py is unchanged and runs a second time on that subset. build_contexts_P.py now resolves a relative chat_template_path against the manifest directory. It also judges validity and cleanliness with the same PREREG_v2 malformed criterion as sample_pools_v2.py. Tested on a synthetic 70-context corpus (scripts/test_P_v11.py, PASS). On the unmodified contexts, v1.1 equals v1.

entries.type: EXPLORATORY bf16 precision row: subset rule pre-declared before any bf16 output (PI constraint)
entries.detail: The bf16 server (gemma-4-31b-bf16 on :8304) keeps about 17k tokens of KV cache, so every request needs prompt + max generation <= 16.4k. The bf16 row is restricted to the S1_A1 states whose longest arm prompt (max over P0/P1/P6/P8a of the QAT run's n_prompt; the bf16 render is identical) is <= 13,000 tokens: 50 of 300 states, 42 episodes (data/confirmatory/bf16_subset_ids.txt). The QAT comparison is restricted to the same 50 states. The runner uses --max_model_len 16400, so max_tokens = min(7168, 16392 - prompt) >= 3,392. On these 50 states, 0 of 200 QAT jobs had prompt + generation above 16.4k (the QAT p99 generation is 2,679 tokens), so the cap would not have bound under QAT. Cap hits are reported. Alternatives considered: full generation parity (prompt <= 9,224) leaves 23 states; thinking budget plus a 1k call (prompt <= 11,272) leaves 32. The A1 median prompt is 16.8k tokens, so most A1 states cannot fit this server at all.

entries.type: operationalisation (S render), decided before any S output
entries.detail: Arm set S renders with enable_thinking=false and appends the template's own closed empty thought '<|channel>thought\n<channel|>' right after the generation prompt. The four appended tokens are 100 <|channel>, 45518 'thought', 107 '\n' and 101 <channel|>; both channel tokens are real special tokens. Evidence: (a) both templates emit exactly this string only when thinking is disabled (June line 351, July line 385); (b) D's anchor no-thought replay (experiments/protocol/order_replay.py without --think) also renders with enable_thinking=False; (c) S is therefore v2.1's render plus the closed thought, i.e. the template's own thinking-disabled form applied at every turn start, including after tool responses, where both templates omit it. All 1,200 S prompts end at '<tool_response|>' before the append, and their last four tokens are the ones above (out/v21_v22_render_check.json). The alternative reading, enable_thinking=true plus the same closed thought, is available as run_cond.py --cond SON. It is not used unless the PI/D decide otherwise before S starts.

entries.type: design fact found before data (v2.1 P5)
entries.detail:
The OFF prompt ends after a tool response in every P0, P1, P6 and P8a context, and in 112/300 P5 contexts. There the June template adds nothing, so the only OFF-vs-ON difference is the system token '<|think|>
' (verified 1,500/1,500). In the other 188/300 P5 contexts the most recent edit call was the last message. P5 removes that call, the template restarts the model turn, and with the flag off it ends the prompt with its own closed empty thought, '<|turn>model
<|channel>thought
<channel|>'. v2.1 is run exactly as frozen. M-v2.1 for P5 is also reported split into template-closed and not template-closed; T4 may carry the 'mixed condition' label (next entry).

A thought is 'opened' when the generated text before '<|tool_call>' (record field s1_text) contains '<|channel>'. Under S this is a re-opening. Thought length is the number of characters between '<|channel>thought\n' and the next '<channel|>' (or the end of the text). The 80% rule (v2.1) and the 10% rule (S) are applied both pooled and per arm: a verdict is labelled if the pooled share, or the share of any arm in its contrast, crosses the threshold. Labelled verdicts are also reported, descriptively, on the contexts where all arms of the contrast opened, or all did not open (S: did not re-open), a thought. One-sided bootstrap p = (1 + #{RD* <= 0})/(B + 1), with B = 2000 and an attempt-cluster bootstrap; Holm families are as registered.

entries.type: fact from already-analysed discovery data (no v2.1 output)
entries.detail: On these 300 gate contexts the thinking-ON runs' thoughts are short. Median characters: P0 80, P1 79, P6 228, P8a 188, P5 593; pooled 185. These mid-trajectory states follow a successful edit. D's 680-character prediction [450, 900] came from B's first-edit replays. H removes reasoning_content and reasoning from every assistant message before rendering, including the corrupted call's own thought under P1. enable_thinking stays true. The June template renders the logged thoughts of the current task segment, so H prompts are much shorter than ON; in the first P1 context, 5,229 vs 13,214 tokens.

v2.1 runs on :8300, as the PI and PREREG_v2.2 state (v2.1's own text says :8302). S and H run on :8302. Both servers have the same non-default arguments as the discovery server (QAT-ct weights, gemma4 parsers, max_model_len 32768, prefix caching), and the generation_config defaults are T 1.0, top-k 64, top-p 0.95. The logged T and top-p are sent per context. Per-context seeds are the discovery ones, giving common random numbers with the ON runs. conc <= 24, --blind. If v2.1 is not finished at 20:30 UTC, its remaining jobs finish on :8302 by resuming the same output file after the :8300 runner stops; there is never more than one writer.

entries.type: PI decision (S render approved) + four-token verification
entries.detail:
The PI approved S as implemented at 17:5x UTC: enable_thinking=false, with the template's own closed thought '<|channel>thought
<channel|>' appended after the generation prompt. SON is skipped, and runs only as exploratory if :8302 has spare time after S and H. Four-token verification with the model's tokenizer: '<|channel>thought
<channel|>' encodes as [100, 45518, 107, 101], i.e. ['<|channel>', 'thought', '
', '<channel|>']. 100 and 101 are the registered special tokens <|channel> and <channel|>, so the thought closes with the real control token. All 1,200 S prompts end in exactly these four ids (out/v21_v22_render_check.json). Both templates emit this string verbatim for thinking-off (June line 351, July line 385). The model's own generated thoughts in the thinking-ON gate runs all open with '<|channel>thought
' (646/646 P0 samples) and close with '<channel|>' (out/v22_thought_form_check.json). Template finding for C and the paper: out/template_thinking_off_gap.md (evidence in out/template_thinking_off_check.json).

entries.type: PI decision before data, per user directive
entries.detail: The optional arms O2 (system-prompt transplant from the main-track contexts) and O1r (reverse transplant on main-track discovery states) are NOT run. The user asked us not to rely on the competition (main-track) work. O1 tests a general property of the public ADK + LiteLLM stack; O2 and O1r would test the team's own setup. Only the primary family O0 vs O1 runs.

O1 construction: every role=tool content c becomes json.dumps({'result': c}, ensure_ascii=False). This is google-adk 1.36.1's own path for a text-returning tool: functions.py:1117 wraps a non-dict result as {'result': value}, and lite_llm._content_to_message_param sends _safe_json_serialize(response). Verified (out/onset_o1_verification.json): equal to the real ADK serializer on 9,211/9,211 tool results of the 600 states. Against C's library-faithful ADK -> LiteLLM 1.104 -> vLLM 0.19.1 pipeline (experiments/conformance/history/pipeline.py, read-only), both the wire tool contents and the rendered tool-response segments are byte-identical on 6/6 states (78 tool results). O0 renders reproduce the logged prompt_tokens on 600/600. Manipulation strength: tool results containing \" rise from 39/9,211 (0.4%) in O0 to 2,959/9,211 (32.1%) in O1, against C's 46.6% rendered and 44-48% logged in the main track. Mean prompt length rises from 13,872 to 14,827 tokens; the maximum is 24,072, so no state lacks room. The comparison with what the main-track pipeline produced uses C's library pipeline and C's documented rates; no main-track log was read (audit).

Outcomes: A's runner judges the FIRST call of the next turn, stopping at the first closed call as in every A battery, so 'the next turn contains an edit call whose value is closed by a look-alike closer' is read as 'the first call is an edit call whose string value contains a look-alike closer followed by ,<declared key>:' (judge closer != None). String-mode drift is measured per state: an edit's new or old string value contains a literal backslash-n or backslash-quote sequence that occurs nowhere in that state's native (O0) tool-result texts. This stands in for 'where the file has none', since file contents are not otherwise available. Each B1 state is its own episode, so the episode-cluster bootstrap resamples states (B = 2000). Scripts were frozen at 07:11:56Z (out/onset_v23_script_hashes.txt).
